articles.title: Bill Oddie Reflects on Rochdale Roots in BBC Documentary
articles.excerpt: Bill Oddie, the renowned television personality, explored his Rochdale heritage in a recent episode of Who Do You Think You Are?, revealing personal family history and its impact on his life.
articles.content_html:
Bill Oddie, the television personality known for his work on The Goodies and Springwatch, recently revisited his roots in Rochdale during an episode of the BBC show Who Do You Think You Are?. Oddie, who was born at Birch Hill Hospital in Littleborough in 1941, moved away from the area at the age of seven when his father secured a job in Birmingham.

In the documentary, Oddie discovered that his ancestors were predominantly mill workers. He learned that his grandmother, Emily Worrall, who played a significant role in his upbringing, was born in Rochdale and likely worked at Arrow Mill in Castleton from the age of 13. Oddie reflected on his complicated relationship with his parents, particularly his mother, who he believed suffered from schizophrenia and was committed to a psychiatric institution during his childhood.

While filming, Oddie met two nurses who cared for his mother, revealing that she was actually diagnosed as manic depressive. He also uncovered the tragic story of a sister who died shortly after birth, which contributed to the challenges his mother faced. This new understanding prompted Oddie to reassess his feelings towards her, expressing regret for not knowing her better.

Oddie's journey has been described as transformative, allowing him to reconcile with his past and gain insight into his family's struggles. He stated, "This journey has been a real lifesaver... I wish I could have done anything about it." His exploration of his heritage has provided him with a deeper understanding of his family's history and its influence on his life.
